GEOMETRY — fixed product position and invariant appearance.
Keep the product at the exact initial frame position shown in Image 1. Preserve its exact pixel width and height, orientation/view, visible faces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette, state, finish and every detail. Build a believable support and room around that fixed product position. Keep exactly one complete, fully visible product. Never move, rotate, mirror, resize, reproject, redraw, crop or occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product.

The table and printer back directly against a plain wall. The operating front faces the camera-side standing aisle.

Camera: A close, slightly elevated, nearly frontal view showing the printer front, top and narrow left side exactly as supplied. Keep zero camera roll. Align the table width edges with the printer’s lower front edge, rising gently toward image right, and its depth edges with the chassis depth direction. Use coherent, restrained perspective throughout.

Composition: Preserve the printer’s exact initial frame position, dimensions and complete silhouette. Construct a sturdy pale oak printer table beneath it, approximately seventy-five centimetres high, with its outer ends cropped by the frame as needed. Keep a shallow clear margin between the printer base and the camera-facing table edge. The mid-plane left tabletop remains empty for sorting papers; add no props or chair. The printer’s back stands right against the wall at the table’s back edge, with nothing between them. A plain dusty blue matte-painted wall occupies the far plane across the left, center and right, filling the broad exposed background above and beside the printer. Below the tabletop, show a modest oak apron, partial legs and a narrow view of warm-neutral flooring. Soft daylight from upper left and generous fill keep the entire station readable.

Remove all gray-guide and diagram remnants and any duplicate product. Render the requested lighting, palette, materials and textures photographically. Keep the product's original color and finish. Match soft, uniform exposure and gentle contrast. Never reproduce diagram lines, boxes, labels, text or flat guide colors.

Build a close office output station around it.
